title: Scalar-current conservation controls the longitudinal current but leaves the transverse near-parallel leakage unchanged

continuity_boundary.bilinear_current: For equal-mass positive-frequency scalar modes k and k+p, take J0=omega(k+p)+omega(k) and J=2k+p at transfer q=(omega(k+p)-omega(k),p)
continuity_boundary.longitudinal_control: The identity fixes only p dot J=(omega(k+p)-omega(k))J0; equivalently it determines the component of J parallel to p
continuity_boundary.transverse_projection: For P_T(p)=I-p tensor p/|p|^2, continuity supplies no condition on P_T J. Every Coulomb polarization e with e dot p=0 obeys e dot P_T J=e dot J=2 e dot k
continuity_boundary.near_parallel_witness: On p=(1,0,0), k=(K,1,0), e=(0,1,0), exact continuity holds while e dot J=2 and the K1468 phase is Theta(K^-2), so the transverse homological quotient remains Theta(K^2)
continuity_boundary.structural_consequence: Adding the time component and the exact continuity identity does not by itself manufacture the Lorentz numerator in the Coulomb-transverse current; a repair must couple another bilinear component, exploit a spacetime estimate, or change the energy
continuity_boundary.ceiling: This excludes continuity alone as the missing transverse cancellation. It is not a no-go for full bilinear decompositions, secondary null forms, spacetime estimates or nonlinear modified energies
